question: Which kind of mirrors is used as rear view wing mirrors in vehicles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Convex mirrors are used as rear view wing mirrors in vehicles because they provide a wider field of view compared to flat or concave mirrors.
 
• This wider field of view helps drivers see more of the area behind and to the sides of their vehicle, reducing blind spots and increasing safety.
 
• Convex mirrors cause objects to appear smaller than they are, which means they appear farther away. This can help drivers better judge the distance of vehicles behind them.
 
• These mirrors are also designed to be durable and resistant to breaking, which is important for external automotive applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors:**

 
 
• Concave mirrors are curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.
 
 
• **Plane Mirrors:**
 
 
• Plane mirrors are flat mirrors that reflect images in their normal proportions, reversed from left to right.
 
• They are commonly used in bathrooms and bedrooms.
 
• Plane mirrors provide a realistic image without distortion but have a limited field of view.
 
• They are not ideal for rear view mirrors in vehicles because they do not cover a wide enough area to be useful for safety purposes.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors are curved outward, like the outside of a sphere.
 
• They provide a wider field of view than plane mirrors, which is why they are used in vehicle wing mirrors.
